lastText: ☰⚙File ClosedThe Fortress Meets the BombMajor DefeatWehrmacht High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: AUTUMN 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathThis was the war that never went east: the deepest projection this campaign contains, since no German planning document ever seriously mapped it: the regime's entire ideology pointed at the decision you cancelled. What followed was a siege, not a campaign. The army history destroyed in Russia stayed intact and unused; the Soviet Union grew stronger every uncontested quarter; and the Anglo-American war arrived anyway, by air and by blockade, against industry it could reach and imports it could throttle. Speer's early dispersal kept industry producing under the bombs and left it to be strangled by blockade instead but the strategic position never changed, because it could not: the fortress had no way to reach the powers besieging it. The Gibraltar gambit staked the Mediterranean strategy on Franco's signature: the campaign's decisive battle was diplomatic, and it was fought in Madrid. The fortified truce held the eastern question at gunpoint: deterrence as permanent institution, the border war that never quite came defining a Europe armed to its median line. In the end, the fortress fought on into the shadow it could not see, and around Autumn 1945 the weapon conceived for Germany was used on Germany (one city, the wait, another) until the same unconditional capitulation arrived by the worst of all available roads.
